issue.title: 🐛 fix(hooks): resolve a literal $ in a relative write path (GH 2451)
issue.body:
## What and why

A `$` that starts no expansion — a trailing `a$`, or the literal `$` in `"$'$HOME'"` — is literal in bash, but the write-path analyzer sent it through raw. `writePaths` then returned an unresolved relative path holding `$`, and `Guard.expand()` returned null for it, so `judgeBash` skipped the line instead of judging it: `cd /etc && touch a$` wrote outside the root unopposed.

The encoder now turns such a `$` into the DOLLAR byte from GH 2443, so the path resolves against the effective cwd and the containment guard judges it. `$NAME`, `${NAME}`, `$1`, `$(` and a backtick are unchanged: they expand or stay UNRESOLVED as before.

## Testing

- `cmd-analysis-literal-dollar.test.js`: 28 pass, including the three new GH 2451 cases (they fail on the unfixed encoder).
- `containment-guard-l3.test.js`: 55 pass, including `cd /etc && touch a$` denied as judged, not skipped.
- `cmd-analysis-l3-write-paths`, `containment-mktemp`, the router parity suites: pass.
- `bash tests/run-all.sh --l1-only`: every step passes except the pre-existing tool-description byte budget failure on dev.
- Full L2/L3 suite: only the pre-existing dev failures (sqlite CLI error-text differences in hook-libs-diff, cli.js integrate, Codex catalog, installed-cache, ensure-swe-worktree, liveness) and load flakes that pass alone.

Closes #2451.

issue.body:
### Addressed Issues:
Fixes #57

### What changed

`_log_gap()` read and rewrote `gap_log.json` with `open()`, `json.load()` and `json.dump()` inside the async function, so every gap entry blocked the Discord event loop for the whole read-modify-write while the lock was held.

Review follow-ups:
- The save is shielded and a cancelled caller waits for the worker before releasing the lock, including when it is cancelled again mid-wait.
- `_load_gap_log()` treats a JSON document that is not a list as corrupt instead of letting `entries.append` raise.
- The lock regression test uses a spy lock to detect the second caller reaching the lock, so there is no fixed wait on the success path.

### Screenshots/Recordings:
N/A — backend event-loop change, no UI.

### Additional Notes:

`tests/test_gap_log.py` uses the stdlib `unittest` (no new dependency) and covers:
- appending and keeping existing entries
- corrupt-file and non-list-file recovery
- 25 concurrent writers losing no entries
- the file I/O running on a worker thread, not the event-loop thread (fails against the old inline code)
- the second call reaching the lock before loading — deterministic, no fixed wait (verified it fails when the lock is removed)
- a cancelled caller keeping the lock until its save completes, including a repeated cancellation (both fail without the shield/retry)

issue.title: Reject Host headers containing commas
issue.body:
### Description

HTTP/1.1 requires exactly one `Host` header line. The C and JRuby parsers merge repeated `Host` lines with `", "`, so `Host: a.example` plus `Host: b.example` currently reaches the app as `HTTP_HOST="a.example, b.example"` with a 200; `SERVER_PORT` can even become `"8080, b.example"`.

This rejects a `Host` value containing a comma in `validate_env`, which already handles the missing-Host case and runs for every parser. That covers both merged duplicate lines and a comma-separated value; valid hosts, including IPv6 literals such as `[::1]:8080`, are unaffected.

One tradeoff: RFC 3986's `reg-name` grammar technically allows a comma, so a single `Host: exa,mple.com` would also be rejected. Catching only merged lines would require duplicate tracking in the C and JRuby parsers; if you would rather keep the reg-name form, I can move the check there.

The first commit adds the regression tests (they fail on main); the second contains the fix, per the bug-fix guidance in CONTRIBUTING.md.

### Testing

- New tests cover duplicate Host lines, duplicate with a port, and a comma-separated Host at both the client-parser and server level, plus a valid IPv6+port case.
- `test_request_single.rb` 100 runs / 321 assertions, `test_request_invalid_multiple.rb` 10 runs / 82 assertions, `test_puma_server.rb` 174 runs / 621 assertions: all pass.
- Rubocop passes on the touched files.
- Full `rake test`: 994 runs, 1 failure and 1 error. Both reproduce on clean `main` too (`TestCategories#test_integration_list_matches_classifier` fails with US-ASCII encoding, `TestPersistent#test_no_chunked_in_http10` fails on the HTTP/1.0 chunked expectation). The flaky `TestIntegrationPumactl#test_stop_unix` also fails on main.

### Checklist
- [x] I have reviewed the contributing guidelines.
- [x] I have added tests.
- [x] This PR is under 100 lines.
- [x] Closes #4084.
- [ ] Documentation is unchanged; this is a parser validation fix.
- [ ] "All tests passed" is left unchecked because of the two failures that also reproduce on main, detailed above.

issue.title: Serialization JSON Schema omits null for an unless-none serializer on an Any field
issue.body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

The 2.14.3 note for #13848 reads "Include `null` in serialization JSON Schema for `unless-none` field serializers", but the code adds it only when the field schema is `nullable`. Fields typed `Any`, `None` or `Literal[1, None]` accept `None` and dump it as `null`, yet their schema stays `{"type": "string"}`, so a generated client rejects that `null`.

The comment at `json_schema.py:515` says the special case "is only relevant for `nullable` schemas", while `WhenUsed` defines `'unless-none'` as "use unless the value is `None`" for any field type.

### Example Code

```Python
from typing import Any, Literal, Optional

from pydantic import BaseModel, field_serializer


class M(BaseModel):
    a: Any = None
    n: None = None
    l: Literal[1, None] = None
    o: Optional[int] = None

    @field_serializer('a', 'n', 'l', 'o', when_used='unless-none')
    def ser(self, v) -> str:
        return f'<{v}>'


props = M.model_json_schema(mode='serialization')['properties']
for k in 'anlo':
    print(props[k])
#> {'title': 'A', 'type': 'string'}
#> {'title': 'N', 'type': 'string'}
#> {'title': 'L', 'type': 'string'}
#> {'anyOf': [{'type': 'null'}, {'type': 'string'}], 'title': 'O'}
print(M().model_dump_json())
#> {"a":null,"n":null,"l":null,"o":null}
```

### Python, Pydantic & OS Version

```Text
             pydantic version: 2.15.0a0+dev (main at fe5b5ce)
        pydantic-core version: 2.50.0
          pydantic-core build: profile=release pgo=false
               python version: 3.15.2 (main, Oct 25 2026, 16:57:51) [Clang 21.0.0 (clang-2100.3.34.2)]
                     platform: macOS-26.7.2-arm64-arm-64bit-Mach-O
             related packages: typing_extensions-4.16.0
```

`object` gives the same result. I would have `_is_nullable_schema` (line 3277) return True for `any` and `none`, and for a `literal` whose `expected` contains `None`. Locally that gives all four fields the `anyOf` that `o` has. Does that match how you read #13848?

I reproduced this on main: `Any`, `None`, `Literal[1, None]` and `Union[Any, int]` fields with a `when_used='unless-none'` serializer get a string-only serialization schema, while `model_dump_json()` emits `null` for them. I have a fix with regression tests on my fork: https://github.com/abu-tahir-0/pydantic/tree/fix/unless-none-null-schema

The contributing guide says an issue must be assigned before a PR is opened. Could this issue be assigned to me so I can submit it? Thanks.

issue.body:
## Problem

`gulliver check --range col=min:max` (and the MCP `ranges` argument) parses each bound with a bare `float()` and pastes the result into SQL. That breaks in three ways:

```bash
# t.duckdb: a table t with a numeric column amount
export GULLIVER_DSN=t.duckdb

gulliver check t --range 'amount=nan:'
# error: Binder Error: Referenced column "nan" not found in FROM clause!

gulliver check t --range 'amount=:inf'
# error: Binder Error: Referenced column "inf" not found in FROM clause!

gulliver check t --range 'amount=abc:1'
# error: could not convert string to float: 'abc'                  <- raw Python message
```

issue.title: analytics: low-severity calculation fixes checklist
issue.body:
Calculation fixes with limited impact: edge cases, labels and secondary statistics. Pick any item; one PR per item is fine. Comment here to say which one you are taking.

## Items

- [ ] intraday::obv_trend: inverted logic on negative OBV values triggers false accumulation divergence (#41) *(good first issue)*
- [ ] bonds::tbill_price: guard against non-positive discount factor to prevent division by zero and negative prices (#57) *(good first issue)*
- [ ] gsec::parse_name: support standard Indian G-Sec query formats 'GSEC', 'G-Sec', and 'GOI' (#58) *(good first issue)*
- [ ] backtest walkforward: out-of-sample trade stats include in-sample P&L (#78)
- [ ] intraday: make "VWAP Reclaim" check a cross and name the VWAP it uses (#79)
- [ ] longterm: the D/E > 250 "dangerous debt" branch can never run (#80) *(good first issue)*
- [ ] derivatives: US option expiry close ignores daylight saving time (#81) *(good first issue)*
- [ ] longterm: Monte Carlo median contradicts the 5-year projection beside it (#82)

## Details

The original issue text, kept here so nothing is lost.

<details>
<summary>#41: intraday::obv_trend: inverted logic on negative OBV values triggers false accumulation divergence</summary>

#### What
In `src/intraday.rs`, Strategy 8 detects On-Balance Volume (OBV) divergence by comparing the most recent OBV reading against its 10-period simple moving average:

```rust
let obv_data = technical::obv(closes, volumes);
let obv_trend = if obv_data.len() > 10 {
    let obv_sma = technical::sma(&obv_data, 10);
    let last_obv = *obv_data.last().unwrap();
    match obv_sma {
        Some(avg) if last_obv > avg * 1.05 => {
            // OBV rising while price might be flat = accumulation
            if regime == MarketRegime::Ranging || regime == MarketRegime::Downtrend {
                strategies.push(StrategySignal {
                    name: "OBV Divergence",
                    direction: Direction::Long,
                    strength: 68.0,
                    reason: "OBV rising (accumulation) despite weak price".into(),
                });
            }
            OBVTrend::Rising
        }
        Some(avg) if last_obv < avg * 0.95 => OBVTrend::Falling,
        _ => OBVTrend::Flat,
    }
} else {
    OBVTrend::Flat
};
```

On-Balance Volume is a cumulative running total of signed volume (+volume on up bars, -volume on down bars). In sustained downtrends or stocks with historical selling, OBV is frequently negative (e.g., `avg = -1,000,000`).

When `avg < 0`:
- `avg * 1.05` equals `-1,050,000` (which is a *smaller* / more negative number).
- If OBV continues to fall from `-1,000,000` to `-1,020,000` (ongoing volume distribution), the check `last_obv > avg * 1.05` (`-1,020,000 > -1,050,000`) is **true**!
- This flags a falling OBV as `OBVTrend::Rising` and triggers a bullish `Long` "OBV Divergence" accumulation signal on a distributing stock.
- Conversely, `avg * 0.95` equals `-950,000`. If OBV actually rises from `-1,000,000` to `-980,000` (real accumulation), `last_obv < avg * 0.95` (`-980,000 < -950,000`) evaluates to **true**, wrongly classifying rising OBV as `OBVTrend::Falling`.

#### Where
- [`src/intraday.rs:404-416`](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/b6268c6f0bdb065b66cba45d0089562bb377341b/src/intraday.rs#L404-L416) — `obv_trend` detection

#### Done when
- The trend comparison accounts for negative values, for example by checking relative change against `avg.abs()`:
  ```rust
  let diff = (last_obv - avg) / avg.abs().max(1.0);
  if diff > 0.05 {
      ...
  } else if diff < -0.05 {
      ...
  }
  ```
- A unit test verifies that negative OBV series correctly identify rising and falling trends.

</details>

<details>
<summary>#57: bonds::tbill_price: guard against non-positive discount factor to prevent division by zero and negative prices</summary>

#### Bug Description
In [`src/bonds.rs:236-244`](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/master/src/bonds.rs#L236-L244), `tbill_price` converts a discount yield to a clean price:

```rust
pub fn tbill_price(yield_pct: f64, days: i64) -> Result<f64> {
    if days <= 0 {
        bail!("the bill has matured ({days} days left)");
    }
    if !yield_pct.is_finite() || yield_pct <= -100.0 {
        bail!("yield must be above −100%, got {yield_pct}");
    }
    Ok(FACE / (1.0 + yield_pct / 100.0 * days as f64 / 365.0))
}
```

The check `yield_pct <= -100.0` only validates that the yield does not produce a non-positive discount factor for a 1-year tenor (`days == 365`). For longer tenors (e.g. 182-day or 364-day bills in extreme yield regimes, or multi-year simulations):
- If `1.0 + yield_pct / 100.0 * days as f64 / 365.0 == 0.0`, the function divides by zero and returns `f64::INFINITY`.
- If the denominator is negative, it returns a negative bond price, which violates bond pricing invariants and panics downstream analytics expecting positive prices.

Furthermore, in [`src/bonds.rs:186`](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/master/src/bonds.rs#L186):
```rust
current_yield_pct: self.coupon_pct / clean * FACE,
```
If a bond has zero clean price (`clean == 0.0`) or is priced at deep discount, `self.coupon_pct / clean * FACE` produces `f64::INFINITY` without checking `clean > 0.0`.

#### Suggested Fix
1. In `tbill_price`, compute the discount factor `denom = 1.0 + (yield_pct / 100.0) * (days as f64 / 365.0)` and verify `denom > 0.0`:
   ```rust
   let denom = 1.0 + yield_pct / 100.0 * days as f64 / 365.0;
   if denom <= 0.0 {
       bail!("yield {yield_pct}% over {days} days produces non-positive discount factor");
   }
   Ok(FACE / denom)
   ```
2. In `analytics_at_yield`, guard `clean > 0.0` before computing `current_yield_pct`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>#58: gsec::parse_name: support standard Indian G-Sec query formats 'GSEC', 'G-Sec', and 'GOI'</summary>

#### Problem
In [`src/gsec.rs:407-431`](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/master/src/gsec.rs#L407-L431), `parse_name` extracts coupon and maturity year from user queries for Indian Government Securities (G-Secs):

```rust
pub fn parse_name(query: &str) -> Option<(f64, i32)> {
    let s: String = query
        .chars()
        .filter(|c| !c.is_whitespace() && *c != '%')
        .collect::<String>()
        .to_ascii_uppercase();
    let (coupon, rest) = s.split_once("GS")?;
    let year: i32 = rest.get(..4)?.parse().ok()?;
...
```

This implementation has two major flaws:
1. **Fails on common market terminology**:
   - `s.split_once("GS")?` strictly matches the two characters `"GS"`.
   - In India, market participants and financial portals frequently write `"7.18% GSEC 2033"`, `"7.18% G-Sec 2033"`, or `"7.18% GOI 2033"` (Government of India).
   - If a user passes `"7.18% GSEC 2033"`, `split_once("GS")` splits at `"GS"`, leaving `rest = "EC2033"`. `rest.get(..4)` extracts `"EC20"`, which fails `parse::<i32>()` and returns `None`.
   - If a user passes `"7.18% G-Sec 2033"`, the hyphen is preserved, so `"GS"` is not found and `split_once` returns `None`.
   - The user receives an unhelpful error:
     `'7.18% GSEC 2033' is not a G-sec name: use an NSE symbol (718GS2033), a name ("7.18% GS 2033") or an ISIN (IN0020230085)`
2. **Brittle two-digit coupon heuristic**:
   - In lines 421-428:
     ```rust
     let two = coupon.len() >= 2
         && coupon.starts_with('1')
         && matches!(coupon.as_bytes()[1], b'0'..=b'2');
     ```
   - This assumes that any two-digit integer coupon starts with `1` and is followed by `0`, `1`, or `2` (10% to 12%). Any coupon >= 13% (such as historical Indian G-secs from the 1990s/2000s or State Development Loans where yields exceeded 13%–14%) fails this condition and gets misparsed as `1.3X%` or `1.4X%`.

#### Suggested Solution
1. Normalize delimiters and synonyms before splitting:
   - Strip hyphens `-` along with whitespace and `%`.
   - Normalize `"GSEC"` and `"GOI"` to `"GS"`.
2. Extract the 4-digit maturity year from the end of the query string and parse the remaining coupon token cleanly with explicit dot placement.

</details>

<details>
<summary>#78: backtest walkforward: out-of-sample trade stats include in-sample P&L</summary>

#### What

Each test window is simulated from the start of its train window so open positions carry in. The code then keeps every trade whose exit date falls inside the test window. A trade opened during the train window keeps its full P&L, its entry costs and its entry price from before the test window started. Those trades feed the out-of-sample win rate, average win and loss, profit factor and costs.

The stitched equity curve is right; the trade statistics printed next to it are partly in-sample. Trade P&L is also not scaled by the window's `scale`, so trade totals don't reconcile with the out-of-sample return.

#### Where

- [`src/backtest/walkforward.rs:181-209`](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/backtest/walkforward.rs#L181-L209) `test_window` filters trades by exit date only
- [`src/backtest/walkforward.rs:318`](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/backtest/walkforward.rs#L318) costs include entry legs from the train window
- [`src/backtest/walkforward.rs:348-352`](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/backtest/walkforward.rs#L348-L352) those trades feed `engine::metrics`
- [`src/backtest/engine.rs:511-515`](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/backtest/engine.rs#L511-L515) `return_pct` from the original entry

#### Evidence

Entry at 100 during the train window, close of 150 the day before the test window, exit at 160 inside it. The out-of-sample equity gains about 6.7%. The trade counts as a +60% win in the out-of-sample stats.

#### Suggested fix

- For a position open at the test start, re-base the trade at the previous close (entry price, basis and `entry_date`), and count only costs of legs inside the window.
- Scale trade P&L by the window `scale`, as the equity is.
- Note in `docs/backtesting.md` how carried positions are counted.

#### Done when

- [ ] Test with the scenario above: out-of-sample `avg_win_percent` ≈ 6.7.
- [ ] Test: with a single carried trade, the sum of out-of-sample `net_pnl` equals the out-of-sample equity change (after costs).

</details>

<details>
<summary>#79: intraday: make "VWAP Reclaim" check a cross and name the VWAP it uses</summary>

#### What

`docs/bots.md` says VWAP Reclaim fires when "Price crosses above VWAP from below". The code fires whenever the live price is 0–0.5% above VWAP and never looks at the previous bar. "VWAP Rejection" fires whenever price is 0–0.5% below.

The VWAP itself is cumulative over the ~21 daily bars of a one-month chart. That is a one-month anchored VWAP, not the session VWAP day traders mean. A stock resting just above that line gets "Price just reclaimed VWAP from below" (strength 75) on every scan.

#### Where

- [`src/intraday.rs:226-245`](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/intraday.rs#L226-L245) VWAP Reclaim / Rejection
- [`src/intraday.rs:869`](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/intraday.rs#L869) data: `1mo` of `1d` bars
- [`docs/bots.md:17`](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/docs/bots.md#L17) documented trigger
- [`src/backtest/indicators.rs:140-155`](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/backtest/indicators.rs#L140-L155) a whole-series VWAP that gives the previous value

#### Suggested fix

- Require a cross: previous close ≤ previous VWAP and price > current VWAP (and the mirror for Rejection), using `backtest::indicators::vwap`.
- Either compute a session VWAP from today's 5-minute bars (one extra request per symbol), or call it "1-month VWAP" in the reason text and docs.

#### Done when

- [ ] Test: price above VWAP on both the last and previous bar → no VWAP Reclaim.
- [ ] Test: a cross from below → VWAP Reclaim.
- [ ] `docs/bots.md` matches the code.

</details>

<details>
<summary>#80: longterm: the D/E > 250 "dangerous debt" branch can never run</summary>

#### What

In `score_for_longterm` the debt checks run in this order: `de < 30`, `de < 80`, `de > 150`, then `de > 250`. Any value above 250 matches `de > 150` first. So the harsher penalty (−20 quality, −25 safety) and the "Dangerous debt levels" flag never fire. A company with D/E 400% scores the same as one at 160%.

#### Where

- [`src/longterm.rs:255-273`](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/longterm.rs#L255-L273) debt branches

#### Suggested fix

Test `de > 250.0` before `de > 150.0`.

#### Done when

- [ ] Unit test: D/E 400 → "Dangerous debt levels" in `risk_flags` and a lower safety score than D/E 160.
- [ ] Unit test: D/E 160 still gets "High leverage".

</details>

<details>
<summary>#81: derivatives: US option expiry close ignores daylight saving time</summary>

#### What

`expiry_close` takes 16:00 New York as 20:00 UTC all year. From the first Sunday of November to the second Sunday of March, New York is on EST and the close is 21:00 UTC. In those months:

- Time to expiry for every US chain is one hour short. For same-day expiries this matters: at 14:30 ET the code uses 0.5 h instead of 1.5 h, which inflates the solved IV by about 70% (√3) and distorts theta and gamma.
- `pick_expiry` treats today's expiry as passed from 15:00 ET, while it still trades for an hour, and silently picks the next one.

#### Where

- [`src/derivatives.rs:246-256`](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/derivatives.rs#L246-L256) `expiry_close`
- [`src/derivatives.rs:260-262`](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/derivatives.rs#L260-L262) `years_to_expiry`
- [`src/derivatives.rs:285-291`](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/derivatives.rs#L285-L291) `pick_expiry` filter

#### Suggested fix

Without new dependencies: the US rule since 2007 is DST from the second Sunday of March to the first Sunday of November. Close at 20:00 UTC during DST, 21:00 UTC otherwise. NSE/BSE stay at 10:00 UTC.

#### Done when

- [ ] Unit tests: 2026-03-06 → 21:00 UTC, 2026-03-13 → 20:00 UTC, 2026-10-30 → 20:00 UTC, 2026-11-06 → 21:00 UTC.
- [ ] `pick_expiry` keeps today's US expiry at 20:30 UTC on a winter date.

</details>

<details>
<summary>#82: longterm: Monte Carlo median contradicts the 5-year projection beside it</summary>

#### What

`longterm` prints a "5-Year Projection" of (1 + est)^5 − 1, then a "Monte Carlo (1000 sims, 5Y)" median. The simulation uses a daily drift of est/252 in simple returns. Compounding noisy simple returns pulls the median down by about σ²/2 a year, so the two numbers disagree for any volatile stock, and the reader can't tell which one the tool believes.

#37 proposes simulating the 5-year endpoint directly; this issue is about which drift that endpoint should use.

#### Where

- [`src/longterm.rs:469-470`](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/longterm.rs#L469-L470) projections as compound growth
- [`src/longterm.rs:538-574`](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/longterm.rs#L538-L574) simulation drift `est_annual / 100 / 252`
- [`src/commands/strategies.rs:685-719`](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/commands/strategies.rs#L685-L719) both printed in one card

#### Evidence

Estimated return 12%, volatility 30%: projection +76%, Monte Carlo median about +45% (exp(5 × (0.12 − 0.045)) − 1).

#### Suggested fix

Pick one convention. If `est_annual_return` is a compound growth rate (as the projections treat it), simulate log returns with drift ln(1 + est) per year, so the median equals the projection. With #37's lognormal endpoint: ln(V₅/V₀) ~ N(5·ln(1 + est), 5·σ²).

#### Done when

- [ ] Test: with volatility 30%, the median is within 2% of the 5-year projection.
- [ ] P10 < median < P90 still holds.

</details>

issue.title: data: small market-data fixes checklist
issue.body:
Small fixes and speed-ups in quote fetching, symbol aliases, caching and error reporting. Pick any item; one PR per item is fine. Comment here to say which one you are taking.

## Items

- [ ] overview: reuse one Yahoo client for the bare-symbol snapshot (#156) *(good first issue)*
- [ ] providers: fetch the NSE, BSE and Yahoo quote legs concurrently (#160) *(good first issue)*
- [ ] views: fetch every markets section in one quote request (#161) *(good first issue)*
- [ ] market: stop the DOW and DAX aliases hiding Dow Inc. and the DAX ETF (#162)
- [ ] market: accept BTC/USD and BTC_USD in the crypto market (#163) *(good first issue)*
- [ ] events: use each exchange's real close when assigning news to a session (#165) *(good first issue)*
- [ ] api: report Yahoo's 404 for an unknown symbol as not found, not a 502 (#167)
- [ ] api: cap the in-memory cache so long-running processes don't grow without limit (#168)

## Details

The original issue text, kept here so nothing is lost.

<details>
<summary>#156: overview: reuse one Yahoo client for the bare-symbol snapshot</summary>

#### What
`stockwise RELIANCE` (a bare symbol, the default invocation) runs `cmd_smart_overview`. It calls `cmd_quote`, which opens its own `YahooClient`, and then opens a second `YahooClient` for the research snapshot.

Each client repeats the cookie and crumb handshake, connects to Redis again, and starts with an empty in-memory cache. So one bare-symbol run makes two extra handshake requests and, unless Redis is running, asks Yahoo for the same quote twice (`research::fetch` quotes the symbol again).

#### Where
- [commands/overview.rs#L283](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/commands/overview.rs#L283) `cmd_smart_overview`
- [commands/overview.rs#L117](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/commands/overview.rs#L117) `cmd_quote` builds a client
- [commands/overview.rs#L289](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/commands/overview.rs#L289) the second client
- [research.rs#L1398](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/research.rs#L1398) the repeated quote request

#### Suggested fix
Split `cmd_quote` into a thin wrapper and an inner `quote_with(client: &YahooClient, ...)`. In `cmd_smart_overview`, build one client and pass it to both `quote_with` and `research::fetch`. Keep today's behaviour that a research failure does not fail the command.

#### Done when
- `cmd_smart_overview` creates exactly one `YahooClient`.
- A bare-symbol run sends one handshake and one quote request (check `api::STATS.requests` or a mock server).
- Existing tests pass.

</details>

<details>
<summary>#160: providers: fetch the NSE, BSE and Yahoo quote legs concurrently</summary>

#### What
NSE and BSE each have their own `Session` and rate limiter, and Yahoo has its own client. Their requests can overlap without being any less polite to each site. Today they run one after another:

- `Exchange::quotes` waits for every NSE quote, then starts BSE.
- `Exchange::search` waits for NSE's search, then BSE's (which may download the scrip list first).
- `YahooClient::get_quote` waits for the provider, then asks Yahoo for the same symbols.

With `STOCKWISE_DATA_PROVIDER=exchange`, a watchlist of 6 `.NS` and 6 `.BO` stocks makes about 12 spaced requests in a row (350 ms plus jitter each), then a Yahoo request. Run together, it takes about as long as the slower exchange.

#### Where
- [providers/mod.rs#L480](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/providers/mod.rs#L480) `Exchange::quotes`
- [providers/mod.rs#L519](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/providers/mod.rs#L519) `Exchange::search`
- [api.rs#L743-L744](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/api.rs#L743-L744) `get_quote`

#### Suggested fix
Use `tokio::join!` in all three places. Keep the current error handling and the request-order output. In `get_quote`, join `provider.quotes(&covered)` with `self.yahoo_quote(symbols)`.

#### Done when
- The three call sites run their legs with `tokio::join!`.
- A test with two mock servers that each delay their answer shows `Exchange::quotes` takes about one delay, not two.
- Existing provider tests pass.

</details>

<details>
<summary>#161: views: fetch every markets section in one quote request</summary>

#### What
`market_sections` sends one quote request per section (home market, the other market, crypto, FX, global) and waits for each before the next. In the middle of the loop it also waits for the India 10-year yield from CCIL or RBI, which has a 6 s timeout.

`stockwise markets --crypto --fx --global` therefore makes five Yahoo requests in a row, each also spaced by the client's 200 ms limiter, plus the yield fetch. The same code serves `/api/markets` and the TUI.

#### Where
- [views.rs#L383](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/views.rs#L383) `market_sections`
- [views.rs#L397](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/views.rs#L397) per-section quote request
- [views.rs#L400](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/views.rs#L400) the yield fetch inside the loop

#### Suggested fix
Collect every section's symbols, call `src.quotes` once, and build each section with the existing `index_rows` (it already matches quotes by symbol, not position). Run `src.india_10y()` at the same time as the quote request with `tokio::join!`.

#### Done when
- `market_sections` calls `quotes` once (a fixture `DataSource` that counts calls).
- Rows and their order are unchanged; existing views tests pass.

</details>

<details>
<summary>#162: market: stop the DOW and DAX aliases hiding Dow Inc. and the DAX ETF</summary>

#### What
`resolve_index_alias` runs before normal symbol resolution in the US, India and global markets. It maps the bare words `DOW` to `^DJI` and `DAX` to `^GDAXI`. Both are also real US tickers: Dow Inc. (NYSE: DOW, an S&P 500 member) and the Global X DAX Germany ETF (Nasdaq: DAX).

There is no way to reach either one. US tickers take no exchange suffix, so the alias wins in `quote`, `history`, `portfolio`, alerts and the API.

#### Where
- [market.rs#L593](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/market.rs#L593) `resolve_index_alias`
- [market.rs#L612](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/market.rs#L612) `DOW`
- [market.rs#L616](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/market.rs#L616) `DAX`
- [market.rs#L1674](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/market.rs#L1674) the test that pins `DOW` to `^DJI`

#### Repro
`stockwise quote DOW -m us` shows the Dow Jones Industrial Average, not Dow Inc.

#### Suggested fix
- In the US market, resolve bare `DOW` and `DAX` as tickers. Keep `DJIA`, `DOWJONES` and `^DJI` for the index.
- Keep `DAX` → `^GDAXI` for `-m de`, where no ticker clashes.
- The benchmark list in `commands/planning.rs` can keep `DOW`, since a benchmark name is not a ticker.
- Mention `DJIA` in the "did you mean" hints so index users find it.

#### Done when
- `resolve_symbol("DOW", Market::Us) == "DOW"` and `resolve_symbol("DJIA", Market::Us) == "^DJI"`.
- `resolve_symbol("DAX", Market::Us) == "DAX"`, and `DAX` in `-m de` still gives `^GDAXI`.
- The old test is updated.

</details>

<details>
<summary>#163: market: accept BTC/USD and BTC_USD in the crypto market</summary>

#### What
In `-m crypto`, a symbol without `-` gets the quote currency appended. `BTC/USD` becomes `BTC/USD-USD` and `eth_inr` becomes `ETH_INR-USD`. Yahoo knows neither, so the user gets "not found".

The FX market already accepts `usd/inr` and `eur-usd` (tested in `market.rs`), and `BTC/USD` is how most exchanges and brokers write a pair.

#### Where
- [market.rs#L660-L661](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/market.rs#L660-L661) the crypto branch of `resolve_symbol_in`
- [market.rs#L1380](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/market.rs#L1380) crypto resolution tests

#### Repro
`stockwise quote BTC/USD -m crypto` asks Yahoo for `BTC/USD-USD`.

#### Suggested fix
In the `Market::Crypto` branch, replace `/`, `_` or a space between two parts with `-` before the existing checks: `BTC/USD` → `BTC-USD`, `eth_inr` → `ETH-INR`.

Optional: split a run-together pair (`BTCUSDT` → `BTC-USDT`) when it ends with a code from `CRYPTO_QUOTES` (longest code first) and at least three characters remain, so `BUSD` and `WBTC` stay as typed.

#### Done when
- Tests: `BTC/USD` → `BTC-USD`, `eth_inr` → `ETH-INR`, `BTC` → `BTC-USD`.
- Existing crypto tests pass.

</details>

<details>
<summary>#165: events: use each exchange's real close when assigning news to a session</summary>

#### What
`reaction_for` decides whether a headline moves today's session or the next one with a fixed UTC hour: 10:00 for India, 20:00 for everything else.

20:00 UTC is 16:00 in New York only during daylight saving time. From November to March the NYSE closes at 21:00 UTC, so news between 15:00 and 16:00 ET is measured against the next session. Global listings (`VOD.L`, `7203.T`) also get the US cutoff, so news after the London or Tokyo close is measured against a session that had already ended.

`clock` already knows each exchange's close, with daylight saving and half days.

#### Where
- [events.rs#L709-L714](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/events.rs#L709-L714) `reaction_for`
- [research.rs#L1420](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/research.rs#L1420) the same `is_india` split also gives global listings the S&P 500 as benchmark

#### Repro
A US headline at 2026-12-01T20:30:00Z (15:30 ET, market open): `reaction_for` picks the 2 December session instead of 1 December.

#### Suggested fix
Pass the symbol's `Market` instead of `is_india` (from `alerts::alert_market`, defaulting to today's rule). Take the local date with `clock::session_date`; if the headline is at or after `clock::close_at(market, date)`, move to the next day. `index_on_or_after` already skips weekends and holidays.

#### Done when
- Tests: a US headline at 20:30Z in December maps to the same day; at 21:05Z to the next day; at 20:05Z in July to the next day.
- An LSE headline after 16:30 London time maps to the next session.
- Existing events tests pass.

</details>

<details>
<summary>#167: api: report Yahoo's 404 for an unknown symbol as not found, not a 502</summary>

#### What
For an unknown symbol, Yahoo's chart endpoint answers HTTP 404 with a JSON body (`"code":"Not Found","description":"No data found, symbol may be delisted"`). `fetch` turns any 4xx into a plain error, "query1.finance.yahoo.com returned HTTP 404 Not Found".

`views::history` only returns its typed `NotFound` when Yahoo sends an empty chart, which it doesn't for unknown symbols. So:

- `GET /api/history/NOTREAL` answers 502 Bad Gateway, which tells clients Yahoo is down.
- The CLI shows the host and status instead of "No price history for X" with the market hint.

#### Where
- [api.rs#L696](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/api.rs#L696) every non-429 4xx becomes a generic error
- [views.rs#L507-L525](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/views.rs#L507-L525) `history`, `NotFound` only for empty bars
- [server/mod.rs#L62](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/server/mod.rs#L62) only `views::NotFound` maps to 404

#### Repro
`curl -s -w '%{http_code}' 'https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/NOTAREALSYMBOLXYZ.NS?range=1mo&interval=1d'` prints the JSON above and `404`. With `stockwise serve`, `GET /api/history/NOTAREALSYMBOLXYZ` returns 502.

#### Suggested fix
In `fetch_uncounted_with`, on 404 return a typed error (for example `api::NotFound` carrying Yahoo's `description`). Let `views::history` and the quote-summary callers convert it to `views::NotFound`, so the server answers 404 and the CLI prints its usual hint.

#### Done when
- A mock-server test: a 404 chart answer makes `views::history` return `views::NotFound`.
- A server test: `/api/history/{unknown}` returns 404.
- 5xx and 429 handling is unchanged.

</details>

<details>
<summary>#168: api: cap the in-memory cache so long-running processes don't grow without limit</summary>

#### What
`HybridCache` keeps every cached response in a `HashMap`. When the map passes 200 entries it drops only expired ones; unexpired entries stay, however many there are.

Some TTLs are long. NSE shareholding XBRL files are cached for 7 days, the shareholding master and corporate actions for 6 hours, fundamentals time series for an hour.

In `serve`, `tui`, `mcp` and `ask`, one client lives for the whole process. Each researched symbol adds its quoteSummary, two two-year charts, time series and up to five XBRL documents, and none of it can be dropped for hours or days. A long MCP or `serve` session that researches many stocks keeps growing.

#### Where
- [api.rs#L187](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/api.rs#L187) `HybridCache::set`
- [api.rs#L202](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/api.rs#L202) eviction of expired entries only
- [research.rs#L1349](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/research.rs#L1349) the 7-day XBRL TTL

#### Suggested fix
Bound the map by entry count and total bytes (for example 500 entries and 64 MB). When it is over, drop expired entries first, then the oldest by insert time. Cap the in-memory TTL (for example one hour) and let Redis, when configured, keep the long-lived copies.

#### Done when
- A unit test inserts more than the cap with long TTLs and the map stays at or under it.
- The most recently inserted keys are still served.
- Existing cache tests pass.

</details>

issue.title: data: small market-data fixes checklist
issue.body:
Small fixes and speed-ups in quote fetching, symbol aliases, caching and error reporting. Pick any item; one PR per item is fine. Comment here to say which one you are taking.

## Items

- [ ] overview: reuse one Yahoo client for the bare-symbol snapshot (#156) *(good first issue)*
- [ ] providers: fetch the NSE, BSE and Yahoo quote legs concurrently (#160) *(good first issue)*
- [ ] views: fetch every markets section in one quote request (#161) *(good first issue)*
- [ ] market: stop the DOW and DAX aliases hiding Dow Inc. and the DAX ETF (#162)
- [ ] market: accept BTC/USD and BTC_USD in the crypto market (#163) *(good first issue)*
- [ ] events: use each exchange's real close when assigning news to a session (#165) *(good first issue)*
- [ ] api: report Yahoo's 404 for an unknown symbol as not found, not a 502 (#167)
- [ ] api: cap the in-memory cache so long-running processes don't grow without limit (#168)

## Details

The original issue text, kept here so nothing is lost.

<details>
<summary>#156: overview: reuse one Yahoo client for the bare-symbol snapshot</summary>

#### What
`stockwise RELIANCE` (a bare symbol, the default invocation) runs `cmd_smart_overview`. It calls `cmd_quote`, which opens its own `YahooClient`, and then opens a second `YahooClient` for the research snapshot.

Each client repeats the cookie and crumb handshake, connects to Redis again, and starts with an empty in-memory cache. So one bare-symbol run makes two extra handshake requests and, unless Redis is running, asks Yahoo for the same quote twice (`research::fetch` quotes the symbol again).

#### Where
- [commands/overview.rs#L283](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/commands/overview.rs#L283) `cmd_smart_overview`
- [commands/overview.rs#L117](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/commands/overview.rs#L117) `cmd_quote` builds a client
- [commands/overview.rs#L289](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/commands/overview.rs#L289) the second client
- [research.rs#L1398](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/research.rs#L1398) the repeated quote request

#### Suggested fix
Split `cmd_quote` into a thin wrapper and an inner `quote_with(client: &YahooClient, ...)`. In `cmd_smart_overview`, build one client and pass it to both `quote_with` and `research::fetch`. Keep today's behaviour that a research failure does not fail the command.

#### Done when
- `cmd_smart_overview` creates exactly one `YahooClient`.
- A bare-symbol run sends one handshake and one quote request (check `api::STATS.requests` or a mock server).
- Existing tests pass.

</details>

<details>
<summary>#160: providers: fetch the NSE, BSE and Yahoo quote legs concurrently</summary>

#### What
NSE and BSE each have their own `Session` and rate limiter, and Yahoo has its own client. Their requests can overlap without being any less polite to each site. Today they run one after another:

- `Exchange::quotes` waits for every NSE quote, then starts BSE.
- `Exchange::search` waits for NSE's search, then BSE's (which may download the scrip list first).
- `YahooClient::get_quote` waits for the provider, then asks Yahoo for the same symbols.

With `STOCKWISE_DATA_PROVIDER=exchange`, a watchlist of 6 `.NS` and 6 `.BO` stocks makes about 12 spaced requests in a row (350 ms plus jitter each), then a Yahoo request. Run together, it takes about as long as the slower exchange.

#### Where
- [providers/mod.rs#L480](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/providers/mod.rs#L480) `Exchange::quotes`
- [providers/mod.rs#L519](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/providers/mod.rs#L519) `Exchange::search`
- [api.rs#L743-L744](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/api.rs#L743-L744) `get_quote`

#### Suggested fix
Use `tokio::join!` in all three places. Keep the current error handling and the request-order output. In `get_quote`, join `provider.quotes(&covered)` with `self.yahoo_quote(symbols)`.

#### Done when
- The three call sites run their legs with `tokio::join!`.
- A test with two mock servers that each delay their answer shows `Exchange::quotes` takes about one delay, not two.
- Existing provider tests pass.

</details>

<details>
<summary>#161: views: fetch every markets section in one quote request</summary>

#### What
`market_sections` sends one quote request per section (home market, the other market, crypto, FX, global) and waits for each before the next. In the middle of the loop it also waits for the India 10-year yield from CCIL or RBI, which has a 6 s timeout.

`stockwise markets --crypto --fx --global` therefore makes five Yahoo requests in a row, each also spaced by the client's 200 ms limiter, plus the yield fetch. The same code serves `/api/markets` and the TUI.

#### Where
- [views.rs#L383](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/views.rs#L383) `market_sections`
- [views.rs#L397](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/views.rs#L397) per-section quote request
- [views.rs#L400](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/views.rs#L400) the yield fetch inside the loop

#### Suggested fix
Collect every section's symbols, call `src.quotes` once, and build each section with the existing `index_rows` (it already matches quotes by symbol, not position). Run `src.india_10y()` at the same time as the quote request with `tokio::join!`.

#### Done when
- `market_sections` calls `quotes` once (a fixture `DataSource` that counts calls).
- Rows and their order are unchanged; existing views tests pass.

</details>

<details>
<summary>#162: market: stop the DOW and DAX aliases hiding Dow Inc. and the DAX ETF</summary>

#### What
`resolve_index_alias` runs before normal symbol resolution in the US, India and global markets. It maps the bare words `DOW` to `^DJI` and `DAX` to `^GDAXI`. Both are also real US tickers: Dow Inc. (NYSE: DOW, an S&P 500 member) and the Global X DAX Germany ETF (Nasdaq: DAX).

There is no way to reach either one. US tickers take no exchange suffix, so the alias wins in `quote`, `history`, `portfolio`, alerts and the API.

#### Where
- [market.rs#L593](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/market.rs#L593) `resolve_index_alias`
- [market.rs#L612](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/market.rs#L612) `DOW`
- [market.rs#L616](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/market.rs#L616) `DAX`
- [market.rs#L1674](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/market.rs#L1674) the test that pins `DOW` to `^DJI`

#### Repro
`stockwise quote DOW -m us` shows the Dow Jones Industrial Average, not Dow Inc.

#### Suggested fix
- In the US market, resolve bare `DOW` and `DAX` as tickers. Keep `DJIA`, `DOWJONES` and `^DJI` for the index.
- Keep `DAX` → `^GDAXI` for `-m de`, where no ticker clashes.
- The benchmark list in `commands/planning.rs` can keep `DOW`, since a benchmark name is not a ticker.
- Mention `DJIA` in the "did you mean" hints so index users find it.

#### Done when
- `resolve_symbol("DOW", Market::Us) == "DOW"` and `resolve_symbol("DJIA", Market::Us) == "^DJI"`.
- `resolve_symbol("DAX", Market::Us) == "DAX"`, and `DAX` in `-m de` still gives `^GDAXI`.
- The old test is updated.

</details>

<details>
<summary>#163: market: accept BTC/USD and BTC_USD in the crypto market</summary>

#### What
In `-m crypto`, a symbol without `-` gets the quote currency appended. `BTC/USD` becomes `BTC/USD-USD` and `eth_inr` becomes `ETH_INR-USD`. Yahoo knows neither, so the user gets "not found".

The FX market already accepts `usd/inr` and `eur-usd` (tested in `market.rs`), and `BTC/USD` is how most exchanges and brokers write a pair.

#### Where
- [market.rs#L660-L661](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/market.rs#L660-L661) the crypto branch of `resolve_symbol_in`
- [market.rs#L1380](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/market.rs#L1380) crypto resolution tests

#### Repro
`stockwise quote BTC/USD -m crypto` asks Yahoo for `BTC/USD-USD`.

#### Suggested fix
In the `Market::Crypto` branch, replace `/`, `_` or a space between two parts with `-` before the existing checks: `BTC/USD` → `BTC-USD`, `eth_inr` → `ETH-INR`.

Optional: split a run-together pair (`BTCUSDT` → `BTC-USDT`) when it ends with a code from `CRYPTO_QUOTES` (longest code first) and at least three characters remain, so `BUSD` and `WBTC` stay as typed.

#### Done when
- Tests: `BTC/USD` → `BTC-USD`, `eth_inr` → `ETH-INR`, `BTC` → `BTC-USD`.
- Existing crypto tests pass.

</details>

<details>
<summary>#165: events: use each exchange's real close when assigning news to a session</summary>

#### What
`reaction_for` decides whether a headline moves today's session or the next one with a fixed UTC hour: 10:00 for India, 20:00 for everything else.

20:00 UTC is 16:00 in New York only during daylight saving time. From November to March the NYSE closes at 21:00 UTC, so news between 15:00 and 16:00 ET is measured against the next session. Global listings (`VOD.L`, `7203.T`) also get the US cutoff, so news after the London or Tokyo close is measured against a session that had already ended.

`clock` already knows each exchange's close, with daylight saving and half days.

#### Where
- [events.rs#L709-L714](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/events.rs#L709-L714) `reaction_for`
- [research.rs#L1420](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/research.rs#L1420) the same `is_india` split also gives global listings the S&P 500 as benchmark

#### Repro
A US headline at 2026-12-01T20:30:00Z (15:30 ET, market open): `reaction_for` picks the 2 December session instead of 1 December.

#### Suggested fix
Pass the symbol's `Market` instead of `is_india` (from `alerts::alert_market`, defaulting to today's rule). Take the local date with `clock::session_date`; if the headline is at or after `clock::close_at(market, date)`, move to the next day. `index_on_or_after` already skips weekends and holidays.

#### Done when
- Tests: a US headline at 20:30Z in December maps to the same day; at 21:05Z to the next day; at 20:05Z in July to the next day.
- An LSE headline after 16:30 London time maps to the next session.
- Existing events tests pass.

</details>

<details>
<summary>#167: api: report Yahoo's 404 for an unknown symbol as not found, not a 502</summary>

#### What
For an unknown symbol, Yahoo's chart endpoint answers HTTP 404 with a JSON body (`"code":"Not Found","description":"No data found, symbol may be delisted"`). `fetch` turns any 4xx into a plain error, "query1.finance.yahoo.com returned HTTP 404 Not Found".

`views::history` only returns its typed `NotFound` when Yahoo sends an empty chart, which it doesn't for unknown symbols. So:

- `GET /api/history/NOTREAL` answers 502 Bad Gateway, which tells clients Yahoo is down.
- The CLI shows the host and status instead of "No price history for X" with the market hint.

#### Where
- [api.rs#L696](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/api.rs#L696) every non-429 4xx becomes a generic error
- [views.rs#L507-L525](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/views.rs#L507-L525) `history`, `NotFound` only for empty bars
- [server/mod.rs#L62](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/server/mod.rs#L62) only `views::NotFound` maps to 404

#### Repro
`curl -s -w '%{http_code}' 'https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/NOTAREALSYMBOLXYZ.NS?range=1mo&interval=1d'` prints the JSON above and `404`. With `stockwise serve`, `GET /api/history/NOTAREALSYMBOLXYZ` returns 502.

#### Suggested fix
In `fetch_uncounted_with`, on 404 return a typed error (for example `api::NotFound` carrying Yahoo's `description`). Let `views::history` and the quote-summary callers convert it to `views::NotFound`, so the server answers 404 and the CLI prints its usual hint.

#### Done when
- A mock-server test: a 404 chart answer makes `views::history` return `views::NotFound`.
- A server test: `/api/history/{unknown}` returns 404.
- 5xx and 429 handling is unchanged.

</details>

<details>
<summary>#168: api: cap the in-memory cache so long-running processes don't grow without limit</summary>

#### What
`HybridCache` keeps every cached response in a `HashMap`. When the map passes 200 entries it drops only expired ones; unexpired entries stay, however many there are.

Some TTLs are long. NSE shareholding XBRL files are cached for 7 days, the shareholding master and corporate actions for 6 hours, fundamentals time series for an hour.

In `serve`, `tui`, `mcp` and `ask`, one client lives for the whole process. Each researched symbol adds its quoteSummary, two two-year charts, time series and up to five XBRL documents, and none of it can be dropped for hours or days. A long MCP or `serve` session that researches many stocks keeps growing.

#### Where
- [api.rs#L187](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/api.rs#L187) `HybridCache::set`
- [api.rs#L202](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/api.rs#L202) eviction of expired entries only
- [research.rs#L1349](https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/research.rs#L1349) the 7-day XBRL TTL

#### Suggested fix
Bound the map by entry count and total bytes (for example 500 entries and 64 MB). When it is over, drop expired entries first, then the oldest by insert time. Cap the in-memory TTL (for example one hour) and let Redis, when configured, keep the long-lived copies.

#### Done when
- A unit test inserts more than the cap with long TTLs and the map stays at or under it.
- The most recently inserted keys are still served.
- Existing cache tests pass.

</details>

issue.title: output: display polish checklist
issue.body:
Small output fixes that make tables, hints and numbers read correctly. Pick any item; one PR per item is fine. Comment here to say which one you are taking.

## Items

- [ ] deep: literal `{}` in 'Income on {}1L' and empty Analyst section (#213) *(good first issue)*
- [ ] news, sentiment: publisher shows raw `url="...">` from Google News (#214) *(good first issue)*
- [ ] display: print index levels without ₹/$ and group digits Indian-style (#217)
- [ ] portfolio: allocation chart is unreadable with NO_COLOR or 8+ holdings (#218) *(good first issue)*
- [ ] rebalance: prints 'SELL 0 shares' and 'BUY 1 shares' (#219) *(good first issue)*
- [ ] hints: fix failing `portfolio lots` hint and add empty-state next steps (#224) *(good first issue)*

## Details

The original issue text, kept here so nothing is lost.

<details>
<summary>#213: deep: literal `{}` in 'Income on {}1L' and empty Analyst section</summary>

#### What
The Dividend block in `deep` prints a format placeholder as text: `Income on {}1L`. The amount is also fixed at one lakh, which means nothing to a US user. Right after it, the "Analyst Ratings" header prints even when none of its fields exist, so the section is empty.

#### Where
- https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/commands/fundamentals.rs#L922-L925 label `"Income on {}1L"` is passed to `print_kv` as is.
- https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/commands/fundamentals.rs#L928-L950 the header prints before the `if let` checks.
- https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/commands/fundamentals.rs#L186-L190 same empty header in `analyze`.

#### Repro
```
$ stockwise deep HDFCBANK
  Dividend
  Yield                        1.86%
  Annual/Share                 ₹13.47
  Income on {}1L               ₹1857/year

  Analyst Ratings
  ────────────────────────────────────────

  Price Chart (3mo)
```

#### Suggested fix
- Build the label with the currency: `Income on ₹1L` for INR and `Income on $10k` for other currencies, matching `divcal`'s `Income on ₹10L`.
- Print the Analyst section only when at least one of `recommendation_mean`, `target_mean_price` or `number_of_analyst_opinions` is present.

#### Done when
- [ ] No `{}` in `deep` output for INR and USD stocks.
- [ ] No empty section headers in `deep` or `analyze`.
- [ ] A snapshot test in `src/commands/output_tests.rs` covers the dividend block.

</details>

<details>
<summary>#214: news, sentiment: publisher shows raw `url="...">` from Google News</summary>

#### What
`parse_rss` in `markets.rs` reads the publisher from `<source url="...">Name</source>`. It looks for `>` followed by a newline, finds no newline, and falls back to the whole tag body. Every Google News line in `news` and `sentiment` then shows the raw attribute. The title also repeats the publisher. The parser in `research.rs` gets both right.

#### Where
- https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/commands/markets.rs#L309-L313 the buggy `between(s, ">", "\n")`.
- https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/research.rs#L1160-L1167 the working version: `split_once('>')`, and the " - Publisher" suffix stripped from the title.

#### Repro
```
$ stockwise sentiment
  ● Share Market Today: Nifty 50, Bank Nifty | Nov 03, 2026 - Liquide Blog
    └ url="https://blog.liquide.life">Liquide Blog · 2026-11-03 11:32 · [Google News]
$ stockwise news TCS        (8 lines like this)
    └ url="https://www.marketwatch.com">MarketWatch · 2026-11-02 10:33 · [Google News]
```

#### Suggested fix
Use `s.split_once('>').map(|(_, name)| name)` as `research.rs` does, and strip `" - {publisher}"` from the end of the title. Better still, move both into one shared RSS helper.

#### Done when
- [ ] `news TCS` and `sentiment` show `└ Liquide Blog · ...` with no `url=`.
- [ ] A unit test feeds `parse_rss` a Google News item with a `<source url=...>` tag.

</details>

<details>
<summary>#217: display: print index levels without ₹/$ and group digits Indian-style</summary>

#### What
Two formatting problems appear on almost every screen.
1. Index levels and VIX carry a currency sign, e.g. `NIFTY 50 ₹23810.85` and `VIX $21.47`. An index is in points. A beginner reads "₹23,810" as a price they can pay.
2. Money has no digit grouping: `₹120092.03 /10 g`, `Total invested ₹305000.00`. The README promises "rupee formatting in lakhs and crores", and `goals::indian_grouping` already exists, but only `goal` uses it. `tax advance` prints `₹2,000` while `tax in` prints `₹125000` on the next screen.

#### Where
- https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/display.rs#L11-L16 `with_currency` adds the symbol and never groups digits.
- https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/display.rs#L34-L37 `format_asset_price` knows `AssetClass::Index` but still adds a currency.
- https://github.com/iamsaquib8/stockwise/blob/e2998d1f4c3528acbb78f8d9106cb9239122c4aa/src/goals.rs#L263-L286 `indian_grouping`, and `western_grouping` below it.

#### Evidence
```
$ stockwise markets
  NIFTY 50         ₹23810.85  ▲ 370.05 (1.58%)
  VIX              $21.47  ▲ 0.32 (1.51%)
$ stockwise commodity spot
               ₹120092.03 /10 g
$ stockwise tax in
  LTCG exemption (₹125000 a year) -₹2000.00
```

#### Suggested fix
- In `format_asset_price`, print `AssetClass::Index` values as plain grouped numbers (`23,810.85`).
- In `with_currency`, group INR with `indian_grouping` (`₹1,20,092.03`) and other currencies with `western_grouping`. Keep JSON and CSV ungrouped.
- Use the shared helper in `tax`, `harvest`, `portfolio` and `xray`, which format by hand today.

#### Done when
- [ ] `markets` shows no currency sign on indices or VIX.
- [ ] INR amounts of ₹1 lakh or more show lakh grouping in tables.
- [ ] Unit tests in `display.rs` cover index, INR, USD and negative values.

</details>

<details>
<summary>#218: portfolio: allocation chart is unreadable with NO_COLOR or 8+ holdings</summary>

#### What
